messages.subject: Defence served - Maybrook v Helmsworth
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

Defence in. As expected: they admit the failures happened but blame our client's misuse and ignored alarms, deny 7.3 is an unqualified warranty, and rely on clause 14.2 (cap £222k, no loss of profit). They also allege failure to mitigate - the 2 June replacement-screen offer.

I'll draft the Reply: deny misuse (scalping screen + magnet), the 2 June offer was for the same defective screen and wouldn't have helped the crusher, and run UCTA hard on 14.2. Targeting service by mid-March.

Kind regards,
Tom

messages.plaintextBody:
Good plan. Make the UCTA reasonableness point the centrepiece - unequal bargaining power, no negotiation of 14.2, and the cap bears no relation to foreseeable loss. Get the expert moving in parallel.
